correctness.rationale: Independence of the squares in a perfect algebra makes the supports of distinct columns of any basis-changing isomorphism disjoint, hence the change is monomial. Since the jth diagonal entry rescales by t_j, normalization is unique and the surviving isomorphisms are simultaneous permutations. Fixed points in the coordinate torus are constant on ordered-pair orbits, and the determinant on the orbit variables has constant term 1 in every characteristic. These fixed loci are dense open in their orbit tori. A permutation preserving each prime-cyclic orbital acts by a translation on each nontrivial cycle (use (x,σx)) and the same translation on every such cycle (use a cross-cycle ordered pair). Thus the orbital constraints of one prime subgroup can only force another if they coincide. Composite orders reduce by taking a prime-order power, proving component maximality of precisely the prime subgroups. Counting fixed pairs and length-p orbits yields the codimension; dividing cycle-type counts by p−1 yields the multiplicity. In the finite quotient fibers are group orbits, so containment of two component images implies containment upstairs in one of the finitely many translates; irreducibility and incomparability give the indexing by (p,r) and finiteness preserves dimension. Only transpositions reach codimension 2n−3; other nonidentity elements move ≥3 vertices and have codimension at least 3n−6≥2n−2. Pairwise transposition intersections impose at least one additional coordinate equality. The fixed-torus counts and degree-n determinant zero bound then prove the uniform leading probability for labelled matrices.
residual_risks: The independent replay verifies finite orbital counts and closures through degree 6 and reproduces all listed prime-field counts using the determinant permutation formula; these do not prove the general geometry or characteristic-uniform asymptotic. The statement concerns ordinary automorphisms, not group schemes or sampling uniformly on isomorphism classes.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct finding is the prime-subgroup component arrangement, with its arbitrary-characteristic codimensions, multiplicities and quotient. The leading density is shared with a later indexed result on the common range of n and is not an independently distinct contribution relative to that record. Neither the inspected literature nor the strongest indexed density match supplies the geometric classification.
residual_risks: Bounded bibliographic coverage, including only the abstract of the Cayley paper; general orbital-closure results for colored digraphs may supply related ingredients. The shared density theorem was found in a later-indexed record; date alone does not determine priority.

value.rationale: The result gives a full geometric description of when ordinary symmetry is possible in a natural algebra parameter space, not just typical rigidity or existence for chosen groups. The component type and codimension also identify which symmetries drive the arithmetic probability.
